scope: Independent review of adapter algebra, synthetic fixture, and global resource guards; no global solve or candidate run.

details: The x-step uses the fused normal LinearOperator and its diagonal Jacobi preconditioner; A^T rhs is cached once through the pinned adjoint.
The ADMM RHS, box/D8/SOC projections, scaled-dual updates, primal/dual/stationarity checks, stopping thresholds, and rho schedule match the pinned CP loop.
Affine d_c and k_g offsets are carried with the same signs as CP. The synthetic fixture compared operator/diagonal and the full solve against CSR/CP.

memory.estimate_status: Approximate array-liveness estimate only; no global process measurement.
memory.reason: The post-solve SOC KKT diagnostic constructs several face-sized float64 arrays plus a 2-column radial array. The adapter does not sample or enforce peak memory during that diagnostic, so the recorded peak can omit its largest transient. Python/allocator and overlapping operator temporaries are not bounded by the small fixture.

time.estimate_status: Lower-bound illustration, not a convergence prediction.
time.reason: Every CG iteration applies the normal operator; actual CG work is multiple iterations across outer iterations. Thus the 3430 case leaves almost no time for other work even under the unrealistically favorable one-CG-iteration assumption, and 5926 already exceeds 1800 seconds at that lower bound.

guard_findings: The timer starts after input-vector conversion/validation, so setup is outside numeric_budget_seconds.

The guard is called at outer-loop entry and CG callbacks, but not around/inside the final projection residual, SOC KKT, and saved-stationarity diagnostics; their time and peak memory are not reliably charged or guarded.
The memory snapshot is sampled at most once per second only when guard executes; postsolve peak can therefore be absent from memory_peak_observed_bytes.
Progress is emitted at iteration 1 and every 200 iterations, not at the requested 25-iteration/30-second cadence.
minimum_changes_before_global_resource_c: Use one deadline that begins before vector conversion and covers all solver and postsolve diagnostics; check it before/after expensive phases.
Sample and enforce peak working set around postsolve diagnostics, especially SOC KKT; alternatively compute that diagnostic in bounded chunks without changing its formula.
Emit a cheap progress record at least every 25 outer iterations or 30 seconds, whichever comes first.
Treat the 1800-second allowance as unproven until a measured representative run or defensible CG-work bound fits it; do not extrapolate from the single normal-action benchmark or 16x16 fixture.

execution_limits.scope_note: The review found no equation mismatch on the inspected ADMM path; the finding is about global runtime/resource enforcement and scaling evidence.
